subject: Prior choice for negative binomial size parameter: pc.mgamma

messages.author: b548117c8aed3bfb
messages.subject: Prior choice for negative binomial size parameter: pc.mgamma
parts:
Hello,
Could someone please help me interpret the mgamma prior for the negative binomial size parameter.
The way I interpret it is that the density is over /theta which can be converted to the negative binomial size parameter as exp(-log(theta)) see R code below for a plot.
It is also not clear to me what the interpretation for the lambda parameter is, though I gather that smaller values of lambda put greater density near zero, whereas greater values will shrink the negative binomial towards a poisson distribution.
Thanks,
Chris


R code to plot priors:

n <- 1000
theta <- seq(0,5, length.out = n)
d1 <- inla.pc.dgamma(theta, lambda = 7) #default?
d2 <- inla.pc.dgamma(theta, lambda = 0.1) #more weight on overdispersion
d3 <- inla.pc.dgamma(theta, lambda = 70) #less weight on overdispersion

plot(exp(-log(theta)),d1, xlab= "negbin size", ylab = "density", type = 'l')
lines(exp(-log(theta)),d2, col = "red")
lines(exp(-log(theta)),d3, col = "green")

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prior choice for negative binomial size parameter: pc.mgamma
parts:
its better to do this



> n = 10^6; delta=inla.pc.rgamma(n, lambda = 7); hist(rgamma(n,

1/delta, 1/delta), prob=T, n=1000)



which gives the distribution for the random scaling factor of the mean
for the Poisson; see the reply to the discussion in the pc-prior paper
in stat sci (see attchment). lambda=7 give a 'reasonable' variability.
we can compute the rate of SD->0 when lambda->infty, but I cannot
recall.


this is the default choice.

hope this helps.
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prior choice for negative binomial size parameter: pc.mgamma
parts:
Hi, 
I wanted help with interpreting and writing the prior distribution for overdispersion parameter and landed on this post.  
Reading throught the document for negative binomial distribution (https://www.inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/likelihood/nbinomial.pdf), I have been writing a GLM mixed effects  model as (this is latex format): 
                y ~ Negative Binomial (\mu , \alpha), 
where \mu is the mean which is the regression model, and variance is \mu(1+ \mu/\alpha). 
However, I am unsure how to write the prior and hyper-parameter distribution for the \alpha.  My interpretation from INLA document is that: 
          \alpha = exp(\theta),
           \theta ~ PC.mGamma (parameter), parameter = 7 (default)

Questions:
1.  how do I write the statistical distribution for \theta?
2. Am I correct to interprete that, 1/\alpha is precision parameter? 

thank you

thanks for sharing that post Dan.
Chris

http://andrewgelman.com/2018/04/03/justify-my-love/
